info.title: Temporal Agents API
info.description: A versioned local API for observing agent work as fleets, standalone run chains, schedules, and a paged active-work projection. The API exposes the work model rather than Temporal or database structures. Writes register places, start work, steer waiting rounds, dismiss finished items, and configure governed prompts. All times are RFC 3339 UTC timestamps. Existing collection reads are capped and newest first. The active-work resource uses opaque source-native cursor pagination. A continue-as-new chain is one item identified by its stable workflow ID. The server binds to loopback by default because responses can contain workflow goals and prompts.

tags.name: Discovery
tags.description: Contract, model, and operational discovery resources.

tags.name: Fleets
tags.description: Orchestrated plan graphs. Fleet status and progress are aggregated by the server.

tags.name: Runs
tags.description: Standalone execution chains. Continue-as-new iterations are collapsed by workflow ID.

tags.name: Schedules
tags.description: Recurring schedule resources. A schedule has no progress and is never dismissible.

tags.name: Places
tags.description: Where the hub may work: places explicitly registered or established by recorded work.

tags.name: Dismissals
tags.description: Durable operator view state over finished items. Dismissals never change workflow state.

tags.name: Active Work
tags.description: A bounded paged projection of unsettled top-level executions and configured schedules.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Signing in with the identity provider, and the session that results. Identity only: this API has no roles and no scopes.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: What the tool is configured to do, resolved through the places work runs in. Each setting reports the scope its value came from, so a consumer never re-derives inheritance.

tags.name: Prompts
tags.description: Governed agent instructions, editable globally and per known place with inheritance and reset.

503.description: At least one dependency is unavailable.

get.description: Returns running fleets and terminal fleets that have not been dismissed. The server aggregates each fleet's node status and progress. Fleet nodes are omitted from this collection; follow a fleet URL for its graph.
Returns a fleet and its plan node graph. Each node carries predecessor links, a server-derived status, and its child workflow execution when it started.

Returns running chains and terminal chains that have not been dismissed. Continue-as-new iterations are collapsed to one item identified by workflow ID. Schedule-fired runs and child workflows are excluded because their schedule or parent represents them.

post.description: Starts one develop or review pass in a place the hub knows. The request names a place and never a path: the server resolves the working tree from its own registry, which is the allowlist of where the hub may work. The request identity makes the start repeatable — the same identity always names the same execution, so a double click, a retried request or a reload ends with one run. A start is refused when work is already running in that place, because two loops in one working tree commit over each other.

201.description: The work that was started. A repeated request identity answers with the run it already started.

get.description: Returns one item per schedule. Status is paused when paused, in-progress while an action is running, otherwise the latest completed action's result, or todo when no action has completed. Schedules have no progress and cannot be dismissed.

post.description: Creates durable view state that hides one finished fleet or run from overview collections. The operation never changes workflow state. Posting the same target again is idempotent because the dismissal identity is derived from kind and item ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The opaque dismissal identifier returned by the create operation.

delete.description: Makes the finished item visible again. It does not change workflow state.

get.description: Returns unsettled top-level fleet and run chains, followed by configured schedules. Source-native opaque cursors keep each request bounded and keep continue-as-new chains stable between pages.

Redirects the browser to the identity provider. The values that bind the callback to this browser are minted and kept server-side; the browser receives one short-lived, script-inaccessible cookie and learns nothing else.

parameters.name: return
parameters.description: Where to send the browser once it is signed in. An application-relative path or an absolute URL on an exact allowlisted frontend origin is honoured; anything else is replaced by /.

303.description: The browser is redirected to the identity provider.

get.description: Where the identity provider sends the browser back to. The code is exchanged server-side; the resulting session cookie is all the browser receives. A callback can be completed exactly once.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The authorization code the provider issued.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The value this server handed the provider, echoed back unchanged.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: What the provider reported instead of a code, when it refused.

303.description: The browser is signed in and redirected to where it was going.

get.description: Answers who the request was made by. It describes the principal and never the credential.

delete.description: Ends the session immediately and clears the cookie. It answers the same way whether or not there was a session to end. DELETE is deliberate: a non-simple method cannot be sent cross-origin without a preflight, so no other page can sign this browser out.

get.description: Every governed setting as it applies to this installation, with the scope each value came from. Resolution walks the place, the repository it belongs to, the installation, and the value this build ships; the server resolves it so no consumer re-derives inheritance.

get.summary: List the places the hub knows
get.description: The union of places an operator registered and places established by recorded work. Registration provenance is null for an observed place. The registry is closed under ancestry, so it contains the same place hierarchy as the work collections.

200.description: The known places, with the registry their references resolve against.

post.description: Records that the hub may work in a directory. The request names a directory and nothing else: what is stored is what the location probe establishes about it, so an operator who names a subdirectory registers the working tree that holds it, and a worktree hangs under the repository the probe names. Registering the same place again returns the registration that is already there.

201.description: The registered place, with the registry its reference resolves against.

post.summary: Open the hub host's native folder picker
post.description: Opens a native directory chooser on the machine that runs the hub. Selection does not register the directory; it returns the absolute path for confirmation or manual editing.

204.description: The picker was closed without a selection.

get.summary: List review rounds waiting for an operator
Read one waiting round and its conversation

200.description: The session, review material, editable guidance, conversation, cost, and contributors.

post.description: Records the first decision durably before resuming the round. A repeat returns the decision that already won.

200.description: The session with the decision that won.

post.description: Appends the operator turn, runs one bounded read-only agent exchange, and returns the durable conversation. Finishing writes the agent output as an editable guidance draft but does not decide the round.

SignInFailed.description: The callback does not belong to a sign-in this server started for this browser, has been used already, expired, or was refused by the provider.

NotAPlace.description: The directory is not one the hub can work in: nothing is there, or no repository holds it.

PlaceIsBusy.description: Work is already running in the place the start names.

NullableTimestamp.description: An RFC 3339 UTC timestamp, or null when the event has not occurred.

locationId.description: The place this item runs, resolved against the response's locations registry.

startedBy.description: Who started the run from the hub, absent for a run started from the command line or fired by a schedule. Published in the single-run representation only.

instructions.description: Which stored instruction the run resolved for each governed key. Published in the single-run representation only.

locationId.description: The place this item runs, resolved against the response's locations registry.

LocationKind.description: The location union's discriminator. A variant carries exactly its own fields.

LocationID.description: An opaque, server-issued location identity. Never parse it: the natural key (the directory, or the ref) is published as a field of its own.

UnknownLocation.description: The place work runs when nothing was recorded about where. It is a real, rendered place: it carries no directory, no ref and no parent.

label.description: The server-computed display name. No consumer derives one from a path.

parentId.description: Always null: the unknown place is a root and has no parent.

DirectoryLocation.description: A place on a machine's filesystem.

label.description: The server-computed display name. No consumer derives one from a path.

parentId.description: The place this one is part of, published earlier in the same registry, or null for a root.

RemoteLocation.description: A place with no local directory, identified by a bounded reference.

label.description: The server-computed display name. No consumer derives one from a path.

parentId.description: The place this one is part of, published earlier in the same registry, or null for a root.

ref.description: The reference identifying the place. It is not a revision: a git ref of a piece of work is an attribute of that work.

Location.description: Where work runs: a closed tagged union of unknown, directory and remote, discriminated by kind.

LocationRegistry.description: The flat registry of every place this response refers to, plus all of their ancestors. Each place appears exactly once, a parent always precedes its children, and the order is deterministic, so a client builds the tree in one pass and an entity tag over the response stays stable. It always contains the unknown place.

conflictingRunId.description: The work a refusal collided with, present only where it collided with something. It is an extension member, so a consumer can link to what is in the way instead of reading an identity out of the detail.

ServiceDescription.description: The API's discoverable entry point. Resource and vocabulary members are intentionally extensible within v1.

status.description: For an execution, the status from the bounded live page. For a schedule, the status from configuration and the last observed completed action.

running.description: Whether the top-level execution is unsettled. Schedule items are configuration and always use false.

locationId.description: The place this item runs. Optional: this model is decoded by existing clients, so the reference is additive only.

next.description: URL of the next active-work page, or null on the final page.

locations.description: Optional here, for the same reason locationId is.

Principal.description: Who a request was made by. Identity is issuer plus subject; the name and the address are display fields and must never be used as identity.

id.description: The stable identity, issuer and subject combined, as an attributed fact records it.

issuer.description: Who vouches for the subject: the identity provider's issuer identifier, or urn:temporal-agents:static-token for the configured automation token.

subject.description: The identifier the issuer uses for this principal, stable across sign-ins.

name.description: The best name available to show a human. Never empty: it falls back to the address and then to the subject.

email.description: The address the provider disclosed, when it disclosed one.

Session.description: The identity behind the current request. It describes the principal and never the credential.

SettingSource.description: The kind of scope a setting's value came from: the place work runs in, the installation, or the value this build ships.

purpose.description: What the setting decides, for a person about to change it.

version.description: Which stored version answered, or 0 when the answer is the value this build ships and storage holds none.

locationId.description: The place, referenced into the registry. The registry is in the collection's envelope, or in this resource's own locations when it is served on its own.

registeredAt.description: When the place was first registered, or null when it is known only from recorded work. A repeat registration does not move it.

registeredBy.description: The principal who registered the place, absent where nobody is authenticated. It is provenance only: the hub has identities and no authorization.

locations.description: Present when the place is served on its own, so its reference resolves without a second read.

directory.description: An absolute, cleaned path of a directory a repository holds, on the machine the work runs on. The place that is registered is the working tree the probe resolves it to.
The absolute directory selected by the native picker on the hub host.

requestId.description: The caller's own identity for this request. The same identity always names the same execution, so repeating a request is not a second run.

kind.description: What to start. A fleet needs its plan approved and a schedule a recurrence, so neither is started here.

placeId.description: The place to work in, as published in a location registry. There is no path field: the server resolves the directory.

prompt.description: What the agent is told to do. Required for a develop pass, refused for a review, which reviews what is already there.

worktree.description: Whether development runs in a fresh server-managed worktree. It never names a path. Refused for a review.

id.description: The run's identity, which /api/v1/runs/{id} answers for once the orchestrator reports it. A start returns before that, so this resource carries what is certain and no invented status.

label.description: What the agent was told to do, empty for a review.

startedBy.description: The principal who started it, absent where nobody is authenticated.

scope.description: Where the value that won came from: "global", "factory", or "directory:<path>".

version.description: Which version of that key and scope answered, or 0 when the value the build ships did.

hash.description: The content hash of the text that was used, so the naming is verifiable. The text itself is deliberately not published here.

PromptSource.description: The kind of scope a prompt value came from.

systemBlock.description: Read-only text appended by the server.

bearerAuth.description: Optional on a loopback-only deployment. Required on every request when the API is reachable from another host.

sessionCookie.name: agent_hub_session
sessionCookie.description: The session a browser receives after signing in with the identity provider. It is set by the callback endpoint, is script-inaccessible, and carries no provider token: the API is the confidential client and holds those server-side.
